desc_en: Qajar steel shield, gold-and-silver damascened; central sun-face boss and four rosette bosses on six-lobed panels engraved with seated courtly figures and musicians; outer band of cartouches with chiselled (pseudo-)inscriptions alternating with bird/animal roundels; brass rim. 340 = plain iron inside with central rivet and four boss rivets
evidence: S-X-001 has four small bosses only, no sun face, all-over arabesque damascening and a red cushion inside — different shield. 340 (plain iron interior) assigned here: shot 2 min after 339, the four rivets in a square around the centre match the four bosses + sun boss; medium certainty since the inside rim edge looks rougher than the brass-rimmed front

desc_en: Hide (buffalo/rhino) shield, translucent orange-brown, gilt sunburst rosette at centre and six gilt lotus-flower bosses on red felt washers; back with red felt cushion, rope/cord handles and iron rings
evidence: No hide shield in catalog; S-X-001 is steel with 4 bosses (back shows dark steel with bright-red cushion and leather straps, not orange hide with faded felt cushion and cord)

desc_en: Steel shield with gold-line koftgari, sixteen-point radiating star/sunburst design, central sun-face boss and four rosette bosses; outer bands densely engraved with nasta'liq inscriptions and animal/hunting scrolls; back lined with red felt with four rings
evidence: S-X-001 front lacks the radiating star and sun-face boss and its back has a separate red cushion with straps, not a full red felt lining with rings; no other shield in catalog

desc_en: Qajar steel kulah khud with mail aventail, engraved with seated figures/courtly scenes, gold koftgari cruciform panels, cartouche band with chiselled inscription round the rim, sliding nasal with heart-shaped terminal, two plume holders and central spike
evidence: S-X-003 is an arabesque/calligraphic silver-gold damascened helmet with nasta'liq band and bird-engraved nasal (no figural scenes); S-X-002 is a plain polished steel helmet with cuirass. This helmet (or a very similar one) is also worn by the mannequin in the mail-shirt shots 375/380/383/384

desc_en: Shamshir with pistol grip of carved bone/ivory (peach-toned, strapwork and quatrefoil arabesques) fixed by two brass pins, plain steel cross guard with ball finials, watered blade with two chiselled cartouches, tang chiselled 'Allah'; black relief-tooled leather scabbard with oval steel lockets and wooden(?) chape
evidence: Rejected S-J-035 (orange flower-carved grip, gilt cartouche guard, tooled brown scabbard) and S-J-043 (carved tan grip with rosette pommel, silver-engraved scabbard locket) after side-by-side comparison; S-J-033/034 have plain ivory grips

desc_en: Short-sleeved riveted mail shirt, open front closing with two leather-and-iron hook clasps, split/scalloped hem; displayed on mannequin with the figural kulah khud and an arm guard
evidence: No mail shirt in catalog (S-X-002 is a plate cuirass). 375/384 fronts and 380/383 backs show identical two-clasp closure, sleeve length and hem split -> treated as one shirt photographed in two passes (18:45 and 19:07); 378/385 clasp close-ups match

desc_en: Long mail shirt with elbow-length sleeves and tall standing mail collar, rust-brown patina, front slit
evidence: Distinct from other shirts: standing mail collar, longer body/sleeves, no clasps visible; no mail shirt in catalog

desc_en: Short-sleeved mail shirt with leather-lined collar, front closing with three iron flower-shaped hook clasps
evidence: Leather collar and three rosette clasps distinguish it; 397 ring close-up shot 15 s after clasp close-ups 395/396 (next shirt starts 6 min later); no mail shirt in catalog

desc_en: Long mail shirt with three-quarter sleeves, keyhole neck opening without collar, ragged hem
evidence: Keyhole neck, no collar or clasps -> different from 375/389/393 shirts; 399-401 close-ups shot within 1 min of 398; no mail shirt in catalog

desc_en: Qajar steel arm guard engraved with figural panels (seated musicians, princes, ladies) under gold-koftgari arches, cartouche with chiselled inscription; plain iron inside (413)
evidence: S-X-005 is a set of char-aina rectangular plates with gold borders and leather straps, not a bazuband; probably the arm guard worn on the mannequin in 375/384

desc_en: Shamshir with ivory grip and steel pommel cap, silver-and-gold koftgari cross guard, watered blade with one teardrop chiselled cartouche with gold outline; plain black leather scabbard with two oval koftgari lockets (floral, gold centre) and long koftgari chape
evidence: Rejected S-J-009 (gold-inlaid nasta'liq on blade, long gilt throat locket), S-J-021/024/027 (tooled leather, steel lockets, no koftgari), S-J-042 (gilt guard, tooled scabbard), S-J-029 (gilt grip mounts)

desc_en: All-steel shamshir, engraved steel pistol grip and cross guard, blade with figural cartouche at forte, long interlaced-calligraphy panel and teardrop cartouche, slotted fuller; black tooled leather scabbard with steel lockets
evidence: Same blade decoration sequence (figure panel at forte, interlaced calligraphic panel, teardrop cartouche, slotted fuller ending) and same engraved steel hilt with conical finials as S-J-046; scabbard not shown in old photos

desc_en: Kard with straight single-edged watered blade and dark iron grip with gold-speckled koftgari; no scabbard
evidence: S-KJ-022 and S-KJ-012 have light wood/bone grips; S-KJ-006 wooden hilt with gilt scabbard; no dark iron-grip kard in catalog

desc_en: Kard with silver hilt and scabbard decorated with blue and green enamel (floral scrolls and inscription), bud-shaped chape finial, straight watered blade
evidence: No enamelled dagger in catalog (S-KJ-008 is plain engraved silver; S-J-041 enamel is a sword)
